mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's own trajectory reversed from a trough of -67.6 at t-2w to -63.9 at t-0w, a sustained two-week improvement. This momentum in the raw mobility series itself, absent any other driver, is predicted to carry forward, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks than the last four.
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the last-28-day mean despite the two-week upward momentum observed at t-1w and t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility fell from 41.1 at t-2w to 38.7 at t-0w, indicating people are spending progressively less time confined at home. Once RESIDENTIAL crosses below a 39.0-point threshold, the freed-up time is redirected into out-of-home discretionary trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 41.1 to 38.7 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL remains below 39.0 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC's mean does not rise relative to the prior four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improved together in the most recent week (WORKPLACES from -66.3 to -60.4; TRANSIT from -67.9 to -64.7). When commuting-linked mobility rises jointly across both series, the combined effect of restored office attendance and transit use generates compounded retail footfall from commute-adjacent errands, amplifying RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series alone would predict over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rose concurrently from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both continue rising together but the four-week mean of RETAIL_REC does not exceed the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: In the most recent week, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, WORKPLACES, and TRANSIT all improved simultaneously, consistent with a coordinated policy-driven relaxation of mobility restrictions. If this reopening regime holds, the broad-based easing should continue to lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as more categories of activity are permitted and resumed.
evidence_refs: fact:all four non-retail, non-residential series improved from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If the regime reverts to tightening (e.g., WORKPLACES or TRANSIT drop sharply in a subsequent week) and RETAIL_REC fails to decline accordingly, or if the broad improvement persists but RETAIL_REC's four-week mean does not rise, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility climbed from -68.1 at t-2w to -63.9 at t-0w, suggesting increased outdoor leisure activity possibly linked to seasonal or weather conditions. This rise in outdoor activity is expected to spill over into nearby retail visits within one week, as people combine outdoor outings with shopping or dining stops.
failure_condition: PARKS continues to rise over the next week but RETAIL_REC's weekly mean does not increase relative to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility rises week-on-week by more than 3 points, as observed from -67.9 at t-1w to -64.7 at t-0w (a 3.2-point jump), this signals a meaningful resumption of commuting and transit-linked errands that produces an immediate, same-week-horizon uptick in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 3.2 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises more than 3 points in a week but the following week's RETAIL_REC mean does not increase relative to the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has stayed persistently elevated, remaining above 38 points for all four observed weeks despite a slight recent dip. As long as RESIDENTIAL stays above a 35-point floor, it indicates households are still substantially confined at home under a lingering restriction regime, which will continue to suppress discretionary retail trips and keep RETAIL_REC's four-week mean lower than the prior period.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has stayed between 38.7 and 41.1 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL remains above 35.0 points throughout the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC's mean nonetheless rises relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both improved substantially in the last two weeks (GROCERY_PHARM from -25.4 to -20.7; TRANSIT from -70.1 to -64.7), jointly indicating that both essential-trip activity and transit-based mobility are recovering in tandem. This combined recovery of essential and transit mobility is a leading indicator of broader consumer confidence returning, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT improved over the last two weeks
